title: TOP-K VIDEOS (YOUTUBE)
subtitle: The design falls straight out of one number: hundreds of thousands of views per second.
footer: DDIA: Ch 11 windows, partitioned streams · Ch 6 partition by key   ·   Similar: Ad click aggregator · Web crawler · Metrics monitoring · Fitness tracking

items: A counter row per video in a database can't take ~800k updates per second.
Stream views through Kafka partitioned by video ID; each consumer counts its videos in memory and keeps a local top-K.
Merge the per-partition top-K lists; the result is exact because each video lives in exactly one partition.
Top K most-viewed videos for the last hour, day, month, and all time
Query latency < 100ms
Freshness ~1 minute
Accurate counts (billing-grade not required, but no big drift)
Massive view volume
70B views/day ≈ ~800k views/s.
4B videos × 8B counters ≈ 32GB of state, spread over partitions.

blocks.text:
GET /topk?window=hour|day|month|all&k=100
view events (video_id, ts) → per-minute counts per video → per-window top-K heap
Naive: increment a counter row per view and ORDER BY views. That is 800k UPDATEs/sec on hot rows, then a full sort.

items: Stream views into Kafka partitioned by video_id, so every view of a video lands on the same consumer.
Each consumer counts in memory in per-minute buckets and keeps a local top-K heap.
Windows: hour = sum of the last 60 minute-buckets (subtract the expiring one). Results are cached; raw events go to S3 for batch correction.
Why is the merge exact?
A video's full count lives in one partition, so its global rank can only come from its local rank. The global top K ⊆ union of local top Ks.
Sliding windows?
A ring buffer of minute counts per video; for months use hourly buckets. Rolling sums avoid rescanning.
Very hot video?
Pre-aggregate on producers (send counts per second, not individual views).
Approximate is OK?
Count-Min Sketch + heap uses fixed memory and is good for trending; exact needs partitioned counting.
A counter row per video in the DB: 800k writes/sec on hot rows.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.

blocks.text: "Stream views through Kafka partitioned by video ID; each consumer counts its videos in memory and keeps a local top-K."
